description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
The Center for Accelerated Women Economic Empowerment (CAWEE) and Resilience joined forces in developing a Tailor-Made Training for female-led businesses in textiles, leather, and agri-food to become export-ready. This was made possible by Nuffic under the Orange Knowledge Program.
The TMT training started with 30 companies classified into three sectors (ten companies per sector) to address Covid-19 measures. We had four companies dropping out during the course due to various (external) factors.
The program started off with six coaches from CAWEE and four trainers/facilitators. The six coaches guided four to seven participants throughout the program implementation period. They also attended half-day training of trainers (TOT) sessions each month for each of the four modules. They then supported the trainees with their homework and training materials, and ensured trainees completed their assignments and presentations on time.
There were four modules each having a specialized trainer/facilitator: (1) business model canvas (BMC), (2) export marketing, (2) export requirements, and (4) pitching and gender. Each module began with a half-day group session to go through the respective course materials, present and review assignments, answer participants' questions, and prepare for the next module. Guest speakers (from Control Union, CBI) were sometimes invited to provide a personal or company perspective on the subject and answer questions the participants had on specific topics (like certification and other market requirements). Each training session was followed by a coaching session to help the company owners and managers better understand the e-learning modules and complete the assignments on time.
26 companies made it through the four modules and to the final pitch competition with five dropouts who did not pitch due to personal reasons. The pitches were evaluated by three external judges from the private sector (one from a Private Equity Company, one from a female-led Bank and one Consultant). In the end ten companies were selected, both on their performance during the course (and quality of their assignments) and their pitch. The ten participated in the in-person trade mission to the Netherlands. In addition to the ten, two representatives from CAWEE also participated in the mission. The larger group was made possible by additional financing from the Embassy.
The trade mission took place in early June, and resulted in 26 meetings. These meetings included visits to workshops and manufacturers as well as importers. In addition, the companies had meetings with representatives from private sector associations, and public organizations (like RVO, CBI and Nuffic). In addition, the group visited a total of 15-20 shops which was part of their market research. Overall, the trade mission to the Netherlands was very successful for the ten female-led businesses; the women gained a lot of knowledge with regards to the Dutch market and the possibility to export their products.
Following the trade mission, a reception was held at the Netherlands Embassy (with the Netherlands Ambassador and Gender Coordinator) to discuss on the participants' experiences and identify potential follow-up activities. The participants expressed that they very much appreciated the organization and content of the trainings and trade mission. They provided many insights on how to improve their products and sales strategy, and start exporting more (e.g., the importance of online sales and marketing was mentioned a lot). The meeting concluded that follow-up activities will be explored both to deepend the current experience and expand the number of participating companies.

comment.narrative: 12-12-2022: After the training program and trade mission we organized a feedback session with the Ambassador and Gender Coordinator of the Netherlands Embassy in Addis Ababa. In addition, we are discussing a follow-up (refresher and echange) program with the Embassy to continue the B2B linkages with Dutch companies and organize a Trade Fair in the Netherlands.

title.narrative: B.I.1. Number of scholarship holders / TMT participants that have successfully completed course/training (male / female / minorities)

comment.narrative: 12-12-2022: Out of the 30 companies 26 completed the courses and trainings, with 21 pitching as the final activity of the training program. In addition, six coaches completed their training and implemented coaching activities. Also, 2 staff of CAWEE participated in the training modules. All 34 received a certificate at the final closing event.

title.narrative: B.O.1. Number of organisations strengthened by individual and/or group training

comment.narrative: 12-12-2022: The Centre for Accelerated Women Economic Empowerment (CAWEE) and its members were the main beneficiary of the training. Through the training the organization received tools on how to organize trainings for its member companies. One of the tools (the Skill-ED e-learning modules) have been made into an App and can be used by CAWEE staff to train more of their member companies. In addition,CAWEE as an organization gained a network with Dutch companies and business organizations (like NABC, TRAIDE Foundation, Dutch women entrepreneurs’ networks) that they can further build on and develop relations for its members.
